title: Verbalized-Confidence Calibration Card for Open Models

original_idea.body: Verbalized-Confidence Calibration Card for Open Models. Problem: LLMs are systematically overconfident when asked to state numeric confidence, clustering at 80-100%. There is no standard lightweight calibration card summarizing an open model's verbalized-confidence calibration on a fixed factual QA set with reliability diagrams and ECE. Direction: on SimpleQA/TriviaQA subsets prompt an open model to answer and state numeric confidence, bin, compute reliability diagrams, ECE, overconfidence index, compare prompt formats, produce a one-page card per model.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (calibration auditing -> honest uncertainty communication -> safer high-stakes decisions) but the step to catastrophic-risk reduction is skipped.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Standard tools (public QA sets, ECE/reliability diagrams), inference-only, beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single artifact with clear success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly external auditing on public models/data; labs have weak incentive to ship standardized cards.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only on QA subsets; single mid GPU or API.

novelty.reasoning: Verbalized calibration is well-studied; the card packaging may be a new angle.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Overconfidence is documented but a standardized calibration-card artifact is plausibly open.
